findings.title: An add during the removal write resurrects the removed instance
findings.trigger: Remove an instance, then submit Add Instance from another tab while the removal's executor write is still running.
findings.execution_path: remove_instance now keeps the old live Settings object intact while awaiting its write. add_instance reads that object and builds new_settings before acquiring search_lock (lines 901–922), so its snapshot includes the instance being removed. Removal then commits and deletes the client, scheduler job, and state entry. The queued add subsequently writes and installs its stale snapshot, restoring the removed instance.
findings.consequence: Both requests report success, but the removed instance reappears in live and persisted settings without its runtime client or scheduler job. Restarting can reactivate it.
findings.evidence: Executed the actual AST-extracted add_instance/remove_instance functions with controlled writer timing and lightweight dependency stubs. Base produced statuses [303, 303], live/persisted ['Default', 'Extra']; head produced statuses [303, 303], live/persisted ['4K', 'Default', 'Extra'], with the removed client absent. Unlike the previously possible pre-lock race acknowledged by plan 87-02, this sequence starts Add after removal already owns the lock and begins writing. Existing concurrency tests pair only removals and therefore miss it.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep write-before-swap, but move add_instance's settings read, validation, and replacement construction inside search_lock. Review save_settings for the same stale-snapshot interaction. Add a regression test that pauses the removal writer, starts Add Instance, releases the writer, and asserts the removed instance remains absent from disk, settings, and runtime registries.
